messages:
earl: RFC idea: adaptive redact levels per route. For high-traffic public routes keep only 64-byte prefixes + hashed fingerprint; for internal admin routes allow 256 bytes. Goal: reduce storage/egress while keeping debuggability. Thoughts?
mei: We need a principled mapping from route -> redact level. Suggest default tiers: public, partner, admin. Admin requires stronger audit.
tom: How does this interact with quota-driven sampling? If a tenant is on a low quota and we sample more aggressively, we might end up storing more prefixes. We should make storage capped per-tenant per-hour.
zara: UX: Console should show redaction tier per-route and a small chart of how many retained events vs cap. Also allow temporary override (canary) for 1h.
dina: Security note: never persist model outputs or embeddings. Also fingerprint must be HMAC with tenant-specific key, rotated monthly.
ear l: (typo) earl: oops, ^ meant 'earl' :) Implementation sketch: router emits metadata: route_id, redact_tier, fingerprint. Redaction middleware applies rules and drops sensitive fields. Example policy: 
```json
{
  "tiers": {
    "public": {
      "prefix_bytes": 64,
      "ttl_hours": 6,
      "store_fingerprint": true
    },
    "partner": {
      "prefix_bytes": 128,
      "ttl_hours": 24,
      "store_fingerprint": true
    },
    "admin": {
      "prefix_bytes": 256,
      "ttl_hours": 72,
      "store_fingerprint": true,
      "breakglass_allowed": true
    }
  },
  "per_tenant_hourly_storage_cap_bytes": 5000000
}
```
mei: +1 but recommend explicit 'no_embeddings' flag at top-level to avoid accidental vector retention.
tom: Ops: we also need backpressure if storage cap hit — i.e., fall back to no-retain and emit a metric. Critical so we don't degrade runtime.
zara: On the console side, when a retain is attempted and cap is hit show a yellow banner: "Retention paused for this tenant until quota window resets" and provide a 'request temporary bump' link.
dina: Legal: any breakglass access must create an audit event including approver id, justification, and auto-redact PII on view. Approvals via SSO; TTL-limited.
sec-bot: security-scan: flagged missing KMS rotation policy for tenant HMAC keys (ticket SEC-4599).
ear l: earl: question about fingerprinting granularity: index on truncated sha256(tenant_key + request_prefix). If we truncate to 12 bytes we reduce index storage but keep uniqueness high. Thoughts?
mei: 12 bytes is OK but document collision risk and rotation semantics. Also add namespace:route to fingerprint to avoid cross-route collisions.
tom: I'll prototype middleware that enforces tier logic + cap and emits metrics: retained.count, retention.denied.cap, retention.fallback.no_store.
zara: I'll mock console visuals for the per-route badge + cap card and share screenshots.
earl: sounds good. If no objections I'll open RFC PR with tests: collision prob test, cap enforcement, embedding-strip test, breakglass workflow e2e.
dina: please link SEC-4599 and include legal wording for the consent/description shown in UI.
sec-bot: canary-deploy: scheduled Thu 03:30 UTC, tag=adaptive-redact-canary
earl: thanks all. followups in thread.
